test_title: PYST 56: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 11 Nov, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

I have __never had__ and never will be dependent on him.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3: never been**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**never been**" is the correct form for indicating that something has not occurred in the past and will not happen in the future, which fits the context of the sentence.

 
 
• **Example:** I have never had and never will **been** dependent on him.
 
 
 
• **"Never been"** correctly connects the two parts of the sentence, indicating that dependence has never existed and will not exist in the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3: never been**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *I have never had and never will been__ dependent on him.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "has never been"** (incorrect): This would be correct in a sentence that focuses on the present, but the structure of the sentence requires "never been" to show both past and future time frames.

 
 
• **Example:** *Incorrect: I have never had and has never been dependent on him.*
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "never has"** (incorrect): "Never has" would not be grammatically correct in this context, as it disrupts the sentence structure and verb tense consistency.
 
 
• **Example:** *Incorrect: Never has been dependent on him.*
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "was never being"** (incorrect): "Was never being" is grammatically incorrect because it combines past tense with a progressive form in an inappropriate way for this sentence.
 
 
• **Example:** *Incorrect: I was never being dependent on him.*
